_comment: Longview Philanthropy public grants (ECF/Longtermism Fund reports, featured grants, US 990 Schedule I), 2026-08-19. Most Longview-advised giving is private; this is the itemizable slice.

grants.recipient: Center for Human-Compatible Artificial Intelligence (UC Berkeley)
grants.description: Supporting graduate students, affiliated researchers, and infrastructure for AI alignment research. Longtermism Fund (now Emerging Challenges Fund) December 2022 grants report.
Funding research scientists, an air sanitisation trial, and establishing a policy unit focused on biosecurity. Longtermism Fund December 2022 grants report.
Supporting researchers and research staff working on existential risk. Longtermism Fund December 2022 grants report.

grants.recipient: Council on Strategic Risks (Nuclear Weapons Policy Work)
grants.description: Policy development, advocacy, and fellowships related to nuclear risk reduction. Longtermism Fund December 2022 grants report.

grants.recipient: Harvard University (Wattenberg & Viegas AI interpretability lab)
grants.description: AI interpretability research: compute cluster setup and hiring graduate students or postdoctoral fellows. Longtermism Fund August 2023 grants report.
Staff costs and possibly compute for assessing whether cutting-edge AI systems pose catastrophic risks before release. Longtermism Fund August 2023 grants report.

grants.recipient: Nuclear Threat Initiative Biosecurity Programme (NTI | Bio)
grants.description: Project to develop research recommendations for disincentivizing state biological weapons programs, including expert workshops. Longtermism Fund August 2023 grants report.

grants.recipient: Center for Communicable Disease Dynamics (Harvard T.H. Chan School)
grants.description: Partially funding the Director of Research and Administration position to support pandemic prevention and biosecurity work. Longtermism Fund August 2023 grants report.

grants.recipient: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace (Nuclear Policy Program)
grants.description: Research workshops and analysis of nuclear war escalation pathways and policy interventions, led by James Acton and Jamie Kwong. Longtermism Fund August 2023 grants report.
Research directions focused on safely building advanced AI systems (robustness, value alignment, model testing, interpretability). ECF December 2023 grants report.

Commissioning research into far-UVC light: efficacy for reducing disease transmission, eye safety, and impacts on air quality. ECF December 2023 grants report. Also listed as a featured grant on longview.org ('Blueprint Biosecurity far-UVC work', added Nov 2023).

Research into nuclear decision-making: sharing and generating research to help officials review nuclear crisis decision protocols. ECF December 2023 grants report. Note: Longview also featured an earlier (pre-2021, amount undisclosed) Decision Research project on psychological processes in nuclear decision-making on its 2021 grantmaking page (https://web.archive.org/web/20210116204242/https://www.longview.org/grantmaking).

grants.recipient: Six EU civil society organisations (aggregate; EU AI Act Emergency Support)
grants.description: Aggregate grant line from the ECF 2024 Annual Report ('$733k, EU AI Act: Emergency Support') supporting civil society organisations invited to help draft the EU AI Act Code of Practice; over half of 2024 ECF grantmaking. Individual recipients not named in the public summary. Three of them are probably the US-entity Schedule I grantees Rethink Priorities ($219,000), Players Philanthropy Fund ($51,000), and AI Objectives Institute ($18,843), each with identical '(AI governance in Europe' purpose text in the FY2024 Form 990 -- see separate 990 entries; treat with care to avoid double counting. Source is the TYPE III AUDIO narration mirror of the (now-unavailable) EA Forum announcement post https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/PBonnCzpMjij4X3Mr/announcing-the-emerging-challenges-fund-s-2024-report; canonical report PDF (download-restricted): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1HIds8PdJsjdMSyW2yQtozqEG87jIOzv9/view

Placing technical expertise in government. ECF 2024 Annual Report grants table. Partially corroborated by FY2024 Form 990 Schedule I grant of $116,285 (general support) from Longview Philanthropy USA Inc; remainder likely disbursed via Giving What We Can/UK entity.
Advising on biosecurity & AI policy. ECF 2024 Annual Report grants table. CLTR (formerly Alpenglow) is also a long-standing Longview featured grantee (see separate entry).

Convening (summary truncated in source; an asterisk footnote on the amount could not be recovered). ECF 2024 Annual Report grants table. Corroborated by FY2024 Form 990 Schedule I: $50,000 to Pacific Forum International, Honolulu HI, 'to support a US-China dialogue to foster mutual understanding and promote public policy development'. This entry and the Schedule I entry are the same grant.

UPDATED 2026-09-03: testing whether cosmic-particle signatures of nuclear warheads could verify compliance with the Outer Space Treaty's ban on nuclear weapons in orbit. Featured (no amount published) as a Nuclear Weapons Policy Fund grant on longview.org, added to the site May 2026, but identifiable as 'Arms Control Verification of the Outer Space Treaty: Feasibility Study' -- a $600,000 first-round award announced 29 Jan 2026 by the Consortium to Reduce Nuclear Dangers, whose press release names Longview Philanthropy among the consortium members supporting this specific award (alongside Carnegie Corporation of New York and other funder(s)). The $600,000 is the Consortium's total multi-funder award for the project, not Longview's share alone. See https://www.carnegie.org/news/articles/consortium-to-reduce-nuclear-dangers-announces-first-round-of-grant-awards-and-welcomes-new-partner/ . Previously recorded here with amount null and date 2026 (year precision, from longview.org alone); amount/date updated now that the underlying Consortium award has been identified.
